name: Question 5
problem: If ${\int }_{C}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-y\,\text{d}y+2z\,\text{d}z$ is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ for some piecewise smooth curve $C,$ then $F(x,y,z)=$
worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)\,i+Q(x,y,z)\,j+R(x,y,z)\,k
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y+R\,\text{d}z
$$

In our case, $P={x}^{2},Q=-y,R=2z.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}({x}^{2}\,i-y\,j+2z\,k)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-y\,\text{d}y+2z\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $F={x}^{2}\,i-y\,j+2z\,k.$

Question 5
?

If ∫Cx2dx−ydy+2zdz is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr for some piecewise smooth curve C, then F(x,y,z)=

a
2xi−j+2k
b
∇(x2−y+2z)
c
12∇(x2−y+2z)2
d
13x3i−12y2j+z2k
e
x2i−yj+2zk
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a piecewise-smooth path C and a vector field F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)i+Q(x,y,z)j+R(x,y,z)k defined on C, we have ∫CF⋅dr=∫CPdx+Qdy+Rdz

In our case, P=x2,Q=−y,R=2z. Therefore

∫C(x2i−yj+2zk)⋅dr=∫Cx2dx−ydy+2zdz.

So, F=x2i−yj+2zk.
